meta.note: Rolling assessment of Aniruddha's interview readiness by skill area. ONE flat dict of skill_areas, one schema per entry. Updated by Claude after each voice/text prep session -- edit entries in place, never append a second JSON object. See CLAUDE.md for update protocol.
meta.rating_rule: 'unrated' means not yet tested in a session. Self-reported or resume-implied skill does not count as rated.

career_narrative_stability.label: Career arc, job-hop story, motivation, what makes him stay
career_narrative_stability.notes: Three short stints (Turing, CES, Espire) explained as circumstantial (funding, wrong team, contract end), not flaky. Problem-driven, not prestige-driven; states a 1-yr floor. Story is credible but rehearse a 60-second version.

ownership_execution.label: Ownership, mentoring, delivering end to end
ownership_execution.notes: Sole owner of Jio recommender; mentored juniors to SDE1. Genuine strength -- turn into 6-8 written STAR stories so it survives interview nerves.

own_projects_deep_dive.label: Defending resume claims with real numbers/architecture (Cellular, Aurora/Pulse, GeoStorm, Jio recommender, Jio ATS, RLHF dashboard, DSA 2.0)
own_projects_deep_dive.notes: Jio recommender: strong -- 100M/day, 33k peak RPS, p50 100ms / p95 200ms, <0.5% errors, named real bottlenecks (GIL, Postgres pooling, network), Kafka + split embedding/similarity services, 700-pod scaling. DataWeave DSA 2.0: partial -- no depth on crawler anti-bot or alerting. Espire (Cellular, Aurora/Pulse), GeoStorm, Jio ATS, RLHF dashboard not yet probed.

staff_leadership_influence.label: Staff-level influence: design docs, driving decisions without authority, org-level tradeoffs
staff_leadership_influence.notes: Not tested. Round 1 surfaced a hint: thinks well at system level, less at org level (versioning strategy, cross-team tradeoffs).

python_core.label: Python fundamentals: GIL, data structures, mutable defaults, copy semantics
python_core.notes: GIL concept ok but missed the concrete release cases (blocking I/O, C extensions like numpy). Mutable defaults nailed. Shallow vs deep copy reversed on nested objects -- must fix. Big-O on containers solid; weak on real-world tuple usage.

python_internals.label: Python runtime internals: MRO/C3, metaclasses, descriptors, attribute lookup
python_internals.notes: MRO/C3, metaclasses, __getattr__ vs __getattribute__ vs __get__ all blanks -- no real exposure. Significant gap for a 'senior Python' bar. Learn via small runnable scripts tied to Pydantic/SQLAlchemy.

async_concurrency.label: asyncio, threading, multiprocessing, structured concurrency, blocking detection
async_concurrency.notes: Event loop concept solid. Unknown: gather vs TaskGroup vs as_completed, structured concurrency, detecting loop blocking in prod (asyncio debug mode, py-spy). Mostly worked in sync codebases. Refresher scripts added in scripts/async/ on 2026-10-10 -- retest R3 Q15-22 next.

web_api_design.label: FastAPI/Flask/ASGI, API error models, request-scoped resources
web_api_design.notes: Practical FastAPI + Pydantic strong. Request-scoped DB sessions (Depends, read replicas, scoped writes) strong. Error model good (codes + Swagger) but missed an explicit retryability signal and calls correlation IDs 'trace IDs'. Gap: ASGI vs WSGI architecture, Pydantic validation cost at scale.

resilience_patterns.label: Rate limiting, circuit breakers, retries/backoff, load shedding
resilience_patterns.notes: Circuit breaker: built from scratch at first job, details faded. Rate limiting: fixed window + sliding log correct, token bucket hazy, no view on edge vs in-app placement. Implement a token bucket once in code.

background_jobs_queues.label: Long-running jobs over HTTP, Celery/workers, job-resource pattern
background_jobs_queues.notes: Job-ID + polling solid; FastAPI BackgroundTasks vs Celery tradeoff clear; real experience with broker/backend split and Flower.

databases.label: Postgres/Mongo/CosmosDB internals, indexing, transactions, isolation, migrations
databases.notes: Not directly tested. Round 1 mentions real Postgres tuning/pooling pain at Jio scale, so expect solid -- but verify isolation levels, index types, EXPLAIN reading, zero-downtime migrations.

caching_redis.label: Redis usage, cache patterns, distributed locks
caching_redis.notes: Everyday Redis (pipelines, caching) fine. Distributed locks / Redlock unknown (R2 Q48 weak). Learn SET NX PX + fencing tokens + why Redlock is contested.

messaging_streaming.label: Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS: models, ordering, consumer groups, DLQs
messaging_streaming.notes: Real TB-scale Kafka. Partitioning, ordering, consumer groups accurate. RabbitMQ for task queues, DLQ, fan-out; clear on when to use which. Not yet tested: exactly-once semantics, schema evolution, CDC (R6 H).

containers_docker.label: Docker images, multi-stage builds, layer optimisation
containers_docker.notes: Multi-stage concept understood but hasn't written a Dockerfile from scratch in 2+ years; wheel-copying and layer ordering hazy.

kubernetes.label: K8s workloads and ops: probes, graceful shutdown, autoscaling, scheduling
kubernetes.notes: Ran 700-pod workloads in prod. Knows SIGTERM + terminationGracePeriodSeconds, but preStop hook (and why endpoints removal races SIGTERM) completely unknown. Wants to build a graceful-shutdown demo himself.

cloud_devops.label: AWS/Azure/GCP, Terraform, CI/CD, multi-region, DR
cloud_devops.notes: GCP + managed services in prod; leaning serverless. No depth yet on multi-region / DR despite StatusNeo Terraform multi-region claim on resume -- must be able to defend it (R1 Q40).

linux_networking_tls.label: Linux, TCP/HTTP, DNS, TLS handshake, load balancers

security_auth.label: OAuth2/OIDC, tokens, RBAC, secrets, AppSec
security_auth.notes: Conflates OAuth2 (authorization) with OIDC (authentication layer on top); access vs ID token unclear. Risky because resume claims multi-provider SSO at GeoStorm (R1 Q28).

system_design.label: End-to-end system design: NFRs, estimation, tradeoffs, failure handling
system_design.notes: No full Round 4 design run yet (log once claimed URL shortener was 'covered in prior session' -- no such session exists). Round 1 shows good instincts defending his own scaling decisions; would rebuild recommender with vector DB + Go + serverless.

distributed_systems_theory.label: CAP/PACELC, consistency models, consensus, idempotency, sagas

ai_llm_rag.label: LLM foundations, RAG design/quality/eval, agents & tool-calling, prod LLM ops
ai_llm_rag.notes: R5 Q22 (RAG debugging): good prod instincts (citations/highlighting in lawyer-doc RAG, retry via smaller guard model) and honest about ranking gap, but missed the core technique (freeze retrieved context, replay to bisect retrieval vs ranking vs generation) and conflated retrieval with ranking. Reranking/cross-encoders taught in-session. R1 confirms production ML is embeddings + vector similarity, RLHF dashboard was ops-heavy. Only ~15 min of real AI questioning so far -- top priority given target title.

ai_infrastructure.label: LLM serving, GPU inference, vector DBs at scale, AI gateways, eval infra
